newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hanwa says unlikely to post loss in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Hanwa says unlikely to post loss in 96/97.

text.p: Hanwa Bank Ltd said it was unlikely to post losses in the current financial year ending next March, despite its announcement on Tuesday that it had revised its forecast for parent current earnings for the first half of the year to a loss of 280 million yen.

The forecast was revised because the bank made loss provisions for loans to a borrower just before it closed its books on September 30, a bank official said. The bank had included the loan loss provision in its earnings forecast for the full year and so there may not be a major change in its previous forecast for 1996/97, he said.
Previously, the company had forecast parent current profit of 60 million yen for the first half of 1996/97.
In the first half of 1995/96, the bank posted current profit of 232 million yen, and 93 million yen profit for the full year.
In May, Hanwa Bank said it forecast 1996/97 parent current profit at 120 million yen.
New earnings estimates for 1996/97 will be announced on November 22 when Hanwa reports its earnings results for the first half, he added.
